newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks seen edging higher, mood cautious.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks seen edging higher, mood cautious.

text.p: Recovering Indian blue-chip stocks are likely to revive the rally sparked by lower interest rates and notch further gains this week but the undercurrent is suspect, brokers and analysts said at the weekend.
"The market has bottomed out," said Jatin Khandwala, a director at Khandwala Finances Ltd, a National exchange broking firm. "I see a 75-100 points rally."
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top-30 share index ended last week 120.45 points, or 3.8 percent, higher at 3,250.66 -- after a 6.7 percent rise in two straight days triggered profit-taking.
Analysts said the quick correction signalled that the euphoria inspired by an easier credit policy was waning.

"Is the recovery going to be sustained?" Narayanan Vaghul, chairman of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, asked at a seminar last week. "Is there an element of threat lurking somewhere there?"
The big rise in share prices was fuelled by expectations of cuts in lending rates, but lower interest rates were old news now, analysts said.
The market motto is: "Buy on expectations, sell on news," said Uday Kotak, vice-chairman of Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd.
The rise was sparked by the central bank's credit policy easing on October 19 which cut cash reserve requirements for banks and lowered the interest ceiling on short-term deposits.
Some main Indian banks cut their prime lending rates to 14.5-15.5 percent in response to the excess cash with them and the lower cost of funds.
Analysts believe the market's fundamental flaws remain -- the almost total absence of retail investors, cash-starved domestic mutual funds, and slowing earnings growth for companies.
"The only thing that has changed is sentiment," said one trader at a big domestic securities firm. "Players have reversed their (short-sold) positions. The big buyers have been foreign funds."

BSE authorities have upgraded 28 stocks to the A group with effect from Monday, taking the total in the section to 60 shares. Trades in A-group stocks can be carried forward at the end of weekly settlements by paying a nominal charge.
"It'll boost liquidity and volumes," said Sushil Parikh, a director at Bombay broking firm K.M. Securities Private Ltd.
Four top firms, Tata Iron and Steel Co (TISCO), Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra are scheduled to unveil their first-half results this week.
TISCO's performance is expected to be hit by poor market conditions, but the other firms are seen riding a boom.
"The results are fully discounted," said Khandwala. "Unless they spring surprises."
